answer: Each total-order sensitivity share must be at least the corresponding first-order share, because total-order includes every interaction involving that input; both indices lie in [0,1]. The first-order shares must also sum to at most 1, with the remainder attributed to interaction and unexplained variance. The book states the sanity conditions explicitly (each first-order index in [0,1]; each total-order index >= its first-order index) and notes that the V12 screen enforces the second by construction, rejecting any screen whose total index falls below a first-order index. In the candidate B example the pairs are 0.361/0.464 and 0.536/0.639, and the two first-order shares sum to 0.897, leaving about 0.103 for interaction and unexplained variation. These are screening sanity checks, not proof of production importance.
